proof_skeleton_nl: First prove the unit-shift identity for F_n. Then iterate it upward to all nonnegative integer shifts and downward to all nonpositive integer shifts. Use the integer decomposition lemma to split an arbitrary z into the nonnegative or negative-successor form, apply the corresponding shift lemma in each case, and finally unfold the notation f = F_n to obtain the exact theorem.

steps.derives: For every real x, f(x + 1) = f(x).
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the conclusion of L1.

steps.derives: For every real x and every natural m, f(x + (m : ℝ)) = f(x).
steps.trivial_justification: The lemma L2 is applied with the unit-shift identity from A1 as its hypothesis, yielding invariance under all nonnegative integer shifts by induction on m.

steps.derives: For every real x and every natural m, f(x - (m : ℝ)) = f(x).
steps.trivial_justification: The lemma L4 is applied with the unit-shift identity from A1 as its hypothesis, yielding invariance under all nonpositive integer shifts.

steps.derives: For an arbitrary integer z, either z = (m : ℤ) for some natural m or z = -((m + 1 : ℤ)) for some natural m.
steps.trivial_justification: This is a direct case split on z using the integer decomposition lemma L5.

steps.derives: In the case z = (m : ℤ), f(x + z) = f(x) for the chosen real x.
steps.trivial_justification: After rewriting z as a natural cast, A2 applies immediately to give the desired equality.

steps.derives: In the case z = -((m + 1 : ℤ)), f(x + z) = f(x) for the chosen real x.
steps.trivial_justification: L3 rewrites x + z into subtraction by a natural number, and A3 then gives invariance under that backward shift.

steps.derives: For every real x and every integer z, f(x + z) = f(x).
steps.trivial_justification: The two cases from A4 cover all integers z; combining the branch conclusions and then universally quantifying over x and z yields the desired statement for f.

steps.derives: For every real number x and every integer z, F_n(x + z) = F_n(x).
steps.trivial_justification: This is just unfolding the notation f = F_n.
